title: The improvement loop: failures become eval cases and proposed prompt versions

story.i_want_to: each spec's recorded failures turned into new eval cases and a proposed next prompt version that must beat the current one on the eval set
story.so_that: the agents improve as they work, and no change to an agent's behaviour ships without measured evidence and a human landing it

rationale: Mark, 2026-11-07: "we need some kind of a feedback loop built-in, so these agents would self-improve as they work." The KB's god-mode cycle (4efb55d0): production runs, traces, new evals, harness changes, run again; and its caution (3b35b25e) that the human stays where 'good' is decided. The PRD keeps prompts on the runner, keyed {id, version}, so an improvement is a new template version landed by PR, never a row an agent writes.

acceptance_criteria.description: spec_tuner@1, a :draft spec, runs weekly per spec with enough outcome rows (threshold in its spec). Its input is the spec's US-48.12 failures (human overrides, budget kills, gate refusals, high review-finding counts) as fenced, untrusted traces, the current template and the current eval set.

Its stored draft (no stage edge, nothing sent) holds: new eval cases distilled from the failures, in the US-48.10 case format with the human's actual decision as the expected answer, and a proposed template revision as a diff against the current {id, version}.

The eval harness (US-48.10) runs current and proposed versions on the enlarged set and attaches both scores to the draft. A proposal that does not beat the current version, or regresses any existing case, is marked rejected and never offered for landing.

An accepted proposal is landed only as a pull request to loopctl-runner (new template version, new eval cases) by a session holding an operator key; loopctl never edits a template or flips a version itself. The spec moves to the new version in the same PR's loopctl counterpart.
MCP tool tuning_drafts lists drafts with their scores and status, in the same change.

test_cases.name: a human override becomes an eval case
steps: record a triage verdict a human overrode
expected_results: the draft holds a case whose expected answer is the human's route

test_cases.name: a regressing proposal is rejected
steps: score a proposal that fails one existing case

test_cases.name: nothing in loopctl changes a template
steps: scan lib/ for writes of a spec's prompt field or a template version

technical_notes: Trace text is untrusted: fenced the same way triage fences reporter text.
The critic that scores proposals is the eval harness, not the tuner's own judgement (KB d7d84a75: a stronger external critic raises the ceiling).
